name: Fried beef meatballs, frozen — Swedish style (קציצות בקר מטוגנות בסגנון שבדי)

source.author: Israeli frozen store product (label photo) — kosher (Kiryat Malachi)
source.notes: Values transcribed directly from the Hebrew label — LABEL-VERIFIED, per 100 g (the label's own basis). Beef 85%. 'Swedish style' = IKEA-style meatball. Fried (refined soybean oil). Iron not on the label; estimated ~2.3 mg/100 g in the analysis only.

ingredients.item: breadcrumbs (wheat flour, gluten, pea starch, yeast)
dietary fiber, spices, salt, sugar, stabilizer (E-450)

steps: Frozen pre-fried meatball — heat through before eating.

him.verdict: Better macros than the chicken version — 19 g protein / 206 kcal (~9.2 g protein per 100 kcal) with only 3 g carb — but worse on the sperm-optimization lens: it's processed red meat, carries 0.6 g trans fat/100 g (trans fat is uniquely worth minimizing for fertility + heart), 4.5 g saturated fat, and 60 mg cholesterol. So it wins if pure cutting macros are the only goal, and loses once sperm optimization is weighted in.
flags: higher protein density (19 g, ~9.2 g/100 kcal)
suggested_mods: If you buy one of the two, the trans fat + processed-red-meat combo makes this the worse pick for your sperm goal despite the better protein
Occasional only; homemade meatballs avoid the trans fat entirely
Air-fry from frozen; pair with veg for fiber

her_preconception.verdict: For her, this edges out the chicken version: red meat brings more iron (~2.3 mg/100 g est.) and more protein (19 g) — both genuine preconception priorities, and the iron matters more than it does for him. The catch is the 0.6 g trans fat/100 g, which is worth minimizing in pregnancy, plus 440 mg sodium. Fully cooked/frozen — safe reheated through.
prenatal_highlights: iron from red meat (~2.3 mg/100 g est.) — supports the preconception iron priority

safety_advisories.note: Contains 0.6 g trans fat/100 g — worth minimizing in pregnancy. Fully cooked then frozen — reheat until steaming.
safety_advisories.swap: leaner non-fried protein where possible; heat through

suggested_mods: Better iron/protein than the chicken version for her; pair with a vitamin-C side to boost iron absorption
Allergens: gluten, soy; may contain sesame, mustard, egg
